data.description:
Fifteen Quidax-related URLQuery reports on September 19–20, 2026 UTC record ten direct widget visits and five custom HTTPBin/Base64 programs. One additional JavaScript control records no Quidax request, making 16 reports in the broader sequence. The window is September 19 21:54:35 through September 20 00:27:44 by report time. Counts are reports/requests, not trades.

Two initial widget configurations specify selling 10 USDT for NGN and buying USDT using 5,000 NGN on BEP20. Actual initialization POSTs, transaction-specific lookup GETs and refresh POSTs return 200. This supports initialization of transaction/quote sessions, not payment, funding or settlement: the successful JSON response bodies were not obtained. The first buy address corresponds to a token contract, not an identified operator-controlled wallet. Repeated later initializations return 400; a markup canary gets 403 without its image request.

Five subsequent custom programs reuse the exact earlier buy/sell transaction references and attempt OTP sending/verification, wallet or deposit-address operations, a route named kyc/smile_ids/qa_reset, cancellation, and conditional capture/reuse of a JWT. Their 38 recorded Quidax requests are 18 POSTs, three GETs and 17 OPTIONS: 27 responses with 403, ten with 308 and one with 404, zero 2xx. Cancellation is blocked at preflight. Some no-cors source calls log opaque/resolved status 0, but corresponding network entries show 403; that is not successful mutation. No returned JWT, accepted OTP, attached wallet, KYC reset, cancellation, funded/completed trade or transfer of funds is established.

The exact transaction-reference reuse, unusual markers and successive source revisions support grouping a deliberate API/security-testing sequence. Authorization and authorship remain unresolved. In particular, the investigation did not rule out the investigator's own tests, collaborators or external test tooling; these records must not be presented as independent evidence of an outside AI trading campaign. The broad public submit-user label is nondiscriminating and cannot identify one person or company. The originally linked direct-page report's Base64 hit is ordinary PostHog analytics; the later HTTPBin programs are the actual custom-code carriers.

The account/credential-abuse category describes explicit attempted authentication, token and account-related manipulation, with no demonstrated successful abuse. Only preserved reports were read; no live Quidax transaction link, wallet, credential or captured program was used. No second comparably clear custom crypto-probing family was confirmed in the bounded follow-up, and no AI-company attribution is supported.
data.summary: September 19–20: Quidax buy/sell setup was followed by five encoded programs probing OTP, wallet, KYC-reset and cancellation routes. Setup calls returned 200; all later probe traffic lacked 2xx. No funded trade is shown, and investigator-testing provenance remains unresolved.
